vulnerabilities: Domestic fiscal and inequality pressures constrain sustained defence modernisation spending
Underinvested blue-water naval capability relative to the length of its Atlantic coastline and offshore pre-salt oil infrastructure it must protect
International pressure over Amazon deforestation creates recurring diplomatic friction with the EU and US that Brazil must manage alongside its economic interests
Domestic security challenges (organised crime, urban violence) draw military and police resources inward rather than toward external power projection
strengths: Largest economy and population in South America, anchoring regional diplomatic and economic leadership (Mercosur)
Energy self-sufficiency and a net oil exporter following the pre-salt offshore discoveries
Custodian of the majority of the Amazon rainforest, giving Brazil unique leverage in global climate diplomacy and negotiations
Non-aligned 'Global South' diplomatic positioning (BRICS founding member) gives Brazil a mediating voice distinct from either US or China blocs
